question: What does IEC stand for in public health?
explanation: IEC is a classic public health strategy combining information sharing, educational activities, and communication channels to promote health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why are IEC materials primarily used in primary health care centers?

options.A: To replace the need for physical doctors and trained nurses in rural posts
options.B: To provide strict legal guidelines for treating infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: To serve as official administrative records for government health budgets
options.D: To help bridge the gap between medical science and community understanding

explanation: Primary health care relies on these materials to translate complex clinical concepts into accessible ideas for everyday people. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h1)

question: A poster featuring local community leaders endorsing immunization improves what aspect of the material?
explanation: Endorsements from respected figures increase community confidence and acceptance of the health message being shared. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why do IEC materials fail when they depict settings foreign to the local population?

options.A: The audience struggles to see the personal relevance of the message
options.B: The local language translation becomes impossible to read
options.C: The printing ink fades much faster under tropical sunlight
options.D: The government health ministry automatically rejects foreign designs

explanation: People connect better with health messages when the visual context mirrors their own everyday environment and experiences. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of relying entirely on heavy text in Nigerian community health materials?

options.A: Lack of available translators for English text
options.B: Strict government laws against printed pamphlets
options.C: Low literacy rates in many rural areas
options.D: High cost of importing colored printing ink

explanation: When communities have low literacy, text-heavy materials fail to communicate, requiring illustrations and verbal reinforcement. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why must nurses avoid direct literal translations when preparing local language health pamphlets?

options.A: Local languages do not contain any words related to modern nursing practice
options.B: Government printing standards require all official posters to remain in English
options.C: Translated words always take up twice as much physical space on paper
options.D: Literal translations can change clinical meanings and sound unnatural to locals

explanation: Idioms and health concepts do not always translate word-for-word, which can lead to confusion or misunderstanding. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary design rule when creating an effective health education poster?

options.A: Fill all empty space with detailed paragraphs
options.B: Focus on one clear, actionable message
options.C: Use at least ten different bright colors
options.D: Include as many health topics as possible to save costs

explanation: Cluttered materials overwhelm readers, whereas a single focused message is easily remembered and acted upon. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why should a health poster for malaria prevention feature a properly hung mosquito net rather than a torn one?

options.A: Torn nets cost more money for the health clinic to purchase
options.B: Visuals should clearly depict the desired positive behavior
options.C: Patients cannot recognize household nets unless they are brand new
options.D: Government regulations ban the printing of damaged household items

explanation: Showing the correct action reinforces the exact behavior change the nurse wants the patient to adopt. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is pre-testing in the context of developing health education materials?

options.A: Sharing draft materials with the target audience before mass printing
options.B: Checking the physical durability of paper under heavy rainfall
options.C: Evaluating nursing students on their graphic design skills
options.D: Testing patients for malaria before giving them mosquito nets

explanation: Pre-testing allows developers to catch errors and cultural misunderstandings before spending money on mass production. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why is community participation essential during the creation of health communication materials?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any professional health staff input
options.B: It ensures the materials meet international printing standards
options.C: It guarantees free distribution through local transport unions
options.D: It helps identify hidden cultural taboos and confusing illustrations

explanation: Local involvement uncovers subtle context issues that outside health workers might easily overlook. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h5)

question: What do Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) surveys help measure regarding IEC materials?

options.A: The grammatical correctness of translated local sentences
options.B: The actual impact of the communication on the target audience
options.C: The exact cost of printing paper and ink in local markets
options.D: The speed at which health workers distribute flyers

explanation: KAP surveys evaluate whether the materials successfully altered what people know, feel, and do regarding health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why must nurses evaluate an IEC campaign even after distributing thousands of posters?

options.A: Printed paper naturally decays quickly in tropical weather conditions
options.B: Health clinics must justify their transport budgets to international donors
options.C: Government policy requires destroying old posters every six months
options.D: Distribution does not automatically mean the message changed health behaviors

explanation: Handing out materials is a logistical step, but true effectiveness is measured by sustained behavioral change. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h6)
